findings.summary: Petri-net causal semantics and causal/event-structure formalisms explicitly represent transition dependencies, token-specific causal histories, concurrency and conflict. Historical token identity plus competition/conflict is therefore an ordinary formal reduction target rather than a novelty axis by itself.
sources: van Glabbeek, Goltz & Schicke, On Causal Semantics of Petri Nets, arXiv:2103.00729 (2021)
Melgratti, Mezzina & Pinna, Relating Reversible Petri Nets and Reversible Event Structures, categorically, LMCS 21(2:20), 2025

findings.summary: Causally consistent dynamic slicing supplies an ordinary actual-run influence baseline between ancestry/provenance and full counterfactual actual causality. A future Spark lineage claim that exceeds ancestor lookup but is exactly recovered by a dynamic slice remains reducible to trace dependence.
sources: Perera, Garg & Cheney, Causally Consistent Dynamic Slicing, CONCUR 2016, DOI 10.4230/LIPIcs.CONCUR.2016.18

findings.summary: GLE and SAL show that fully local/online physical or spiking credit machinery is a populated contemporary mechanism class. Locality, online operation, spiking implementation, or history-sensitive plasticity cannot independently support SparkBrain novelty; any residual must be lineage-selective and intervention-validated under matched local information.
sources: Backpropagation through space, time and the brain, Nature Communications 17, Article 66 (2026), DOI 10.1038/s41467-025-66666-z
Gierlich et al., Spike-based alignment learning solves the weight transport problem, Nature Communications 17, 8699 (2026), DOI 10.1038/s41467-026-74460-8
